identification.summary: UTA0388 is Volexity's name for a China-aligned cluster known for spear-phishing against organizations in North America, Asia and Europe, primarily to deliver a Go-based implant Volexity calls GOVERSHELL [S1][S2]. Volexity's earliest GOVERSHELL variant is the HealthKick family, which Proofpoint associated with a separate cluster, UNK_DropPitch [S2][S5]. Volexity assessed with medium confidence that the actor used LLMs or automation in its operations [S1][S2]. OpenAI separately reported banning ChatGPT accounts whose activity overlapped public reporting on UNK_DROPPITCH and UTA0388 [S3].
identification.firstObserved: Hive Pro reports first observation in March 2025 [S4]. Volexity's initially detected campaign window was June to August 2025 [S4].
identification.notes: Volexity primary name: UTA0388 (UTA = unattributed). No Microsoft Threat Actor name is established in the sources gathered. Also tracked as UNK_DropPitch (Proofpoint) [S3][S4]; the two names are described as overlapping, not identical, so keep vendor cluster boundaries separate. The primary Volexity post could not be opened in this session (fetch failed); facts here rely on secondary coverage of it [S1][S2][S4].

attribution.confidence: Volexity describes UTA0388 as China-aligned, not as a named PRC organization [S1][S2]. OpenAI said the overlapping activity showed signs of cyber operations serving PRC intelligence requirements [S3]. No government attribution was found.
attribution.basis: Reported basis includes Chinese-language use and a Simplified Chinese development environment for GOVERSHELL, plus targeting aligned with Asian geopolitical issues [S1][S3]. OpenAI noted Chinese-language activity and targeting of Taiwan's semiconductor sector, US academia and think tanks, and groups critical of the CCP [S3].

objectives: Espionage consistent with PRC intelligence requirements, per OpenAI's assessment of the overlapping cluster [S3]. Proofpoint researchers suspected interest in emerging information on the Taiwanese semiconductor market, such as new product lines [S5].

sectors: Semiconductor industry analysts and investment firms (UNK_DropPitch, Proofpoint)
targeting.notes: Proofpoint reported UNK_DropPitch striking individuals at multiple major investment firms focused on analysis of the Taiwanese semiconductor industry [S5]. Sector detail for the wider UTA0388 campaigns beyond these items was not verified from the primary Volexity report.

capabilities.summary: Spear-phishing with links to archives (.ZIP/.RAR) hosted on legitimate cloud services such as Netlify, OneDrive and Sync.com, with sender addresses on Proton Mail, Outlook and Gmail [S1][S2]. Lures used fabricated personas and multiple languages [S1]. From about August 2025 the actor used rapport-building, corresponding over several emails before sending the malicious link [S2]. Infection relies on Windows search-order (DLL side-loading) hijacking so a legitimate application loads the malicious DLL [S1][S5]. GOVERSHELL is a Go-based implant that can execute remote commands, gather system data and maintain persistence; Volexity tracked five variants, each described as a significant rewrite [S1][S4]. A secondary summary lists variants as HealthKick, TE32, TE64, a WebSocket variant and a Beacon variant (September 2025) [S6]. Volexity assessed with medium confidence that LLMs were used to craft multilingual phishing [S1][S2]. OpenAI judged the operators technically competent but unsophisticated, noting a simple static key despite discussing stronger C2 encryption, and said models mainly gave incremental efficiency in phishing content and tool debugging [S3].

campaigns.name: Earliest observed activity
campaigns.summary: Hive Pro reports first observation of UTA0388 activity in March 2025 [S4].

campaigns.name: UNK_DropPitch HealthKick phishing against Taiwan semiconductor analysts
campaigns.summary: Proofpoint reported April and May 2025 emails linking to a PDF that fetched a ZIP with a DLL side-loaded to deliver the HealthKick backdoor, aimed at investment-firm analysts covering Taiwan's semiconductor industry. Volexity links HealthKick to the earliest GOVERSHELL variant, but Proofpoint's cluster and UTA0388 are separate vendor tracking names [S2][S5].

campaigns.name: Volexity-detected spear-phishing waves delivering GOVERSHELL
campaigns.summary: Volexity's initial detection window ran June to August 2025, with multilingual persona-based lures and archives hosted on Netlify, Sync and OneDrive; activity reportedly peaked in July 2025 [S1][S4].

campaigns.name: Shift to rapport-building phishing
campaigns.summary: Volexity dates the change to August 2025: after broad campaigns subsided, the actor held multi-email conversations before sending the malicious link [S2].

campaigns.name: OpenAI bans overlapping ChatGPT accounts
campaigns.summary: OpenAI's threat report banned a cluster of accounts overlapping UNK_DROPPITCH and UTA0388; in at least one case a phishing sender used the same email address registered to a ChatGPT account [S3].

campaigns.name: Volexity publishes 'APT Meets GPT'
campaigns.summary: Volexity publication on UTA0388, GOVERSHELL variants and suspected LLM use; coverage says activity slowed from its July 2025 peak but remained a consistent threat [S2][S6].

campaigns.name: CyCraft analysis of UTA0388 against Asia
campaigns.summary: CyCraft published a monthly intelligence piece titled 'Attacking Asia with AI: Analysis of Emerging UTA0388 Threat' (content not reviewed) [S7].

diamond.adversary: China-aligned cluster tracked by Volexity as UTA0388; overlapping with Proofpoint's UNK_DropPitch; operator identities unknown [S1][S3].
diamond.capability: Persona-based multilingual spear-phishing, rapport-building, DLL search-order hijacking, Go-based GOVERSHELL (five variants) descended from HealthKick, suspected LLM-assisted content [S1][S2][S5].
diamond.infrastructure: Archives on Netlify, Sync.com and OneDrive; sender mailboxes on Proton Mail, Outlook and Gmail; actor C2 details not captured [S1][S2].
diamond.victim: Taiwan semiconductor analysts, US academia and think tanks, CCP-critical groups, and organizations in North America, Asia and Europe [S2][S3][S5].
diamond.socioPolitical: Collection supporting PRC intelligence requirements on Taiwan, technology markets and dissent [S3][S5].
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints susceptible to DLL side-loading, email and trusted cloud file-hosting services, and commercial LLM platforms used by the actor [S1][S3].

gaps: Primary Volexity and Proofpoint reports and the OpenAI case text were not opened. Variant names, dates and persona details come from secondary coverage and need checking against the primary [S6].
Relationship between UTA0388 and UNK_DropPitch is described as overlap; the exact boundary is unverified [S3][S5].
No named PRC sponsor, government attribution, or Microsoft actor name was found.
Specific victims, success rate and data stolen are not public in the sources gathered.
C2 domains, IPs and file hashes were not captured.
Whether the group maps to any other named cluster (for example MITRE group) is unknown.
CyCraft's December 2025 analysis was not reviewed [S7].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is personnel email and collaboration accounts of analysts, academics and policy staff, plus trusted cloud file-hosting services the actor abuses [S1][S2]. STEP 2: The actor blends in using legitimate cloud hosting, free mail providers and conversational rapport, which defeats reputation filtering and user training aimed at one-shot phishing [S2]. STEP 3: Template is persona email, then rapport, then cloud-hosted archive, then DLL side-loading, then GOVERSHELL command execution [S1][S2][S5]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued low-volume targeted phishing of Taiwan-related, think-tank and academic personnel for intelligence collection [S3][S5]. MDCOA is the same tradecraft aimed at DoD-adjacent or INDOPACOM-related staff and contractors, with LLMs scaling multilingual lures [S1][S3]. Candidate indicators: unsolicited correspondence from new personas on free mail services escalating to archive links; downloads from Netlify, Sync or OneDrive of ZIP/RAR files; legitimate executables loading unexpected DLLs from user-writable folders [S1][S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track vendor reporting on UTA0388 and UNK_DropPitch as possibly related but distinct clusters, and avoid merging indicators [S3][S5]. (2) Authorities: monitoring of personal or commercial mailboxes and cloud-hosting abuse reporting need appropriate legal coordination; blocking of cloud services affects mission users [S2]. (3) Mission assurance: prioritize user awareness for long-running conversational lures and endpoint detection for DLL side-loading on mission systems [S1][S2]. (4) Coordination: share indicators through DC3 and DIB partners, and with Taiwan-focused academic and industry contacts, as the cluster targeted such communities [S3][S5].
